holidays.name: National Taco Day
holidays.description: A crunchy, cheesy, saucy celebration of the humble taco in all its forms, from street-style carne asada to hard-shell ground beef. Restaurants across the U.S. roll out deals and taco fans make a point of eating at least one.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food holiday that grew in popularity in the 2000s and 2010s. Taco Bell later tried to trademark 'Taco Tuesday' and fought over related claims, but National Taco Day on October 4 has been widely embraced by taquerias and chains alike.
holidays.funFact: Tacos have been traced back to 18th-century Mexican silver mines, where 'tacos' referred to little paper-wrapped charges of gunpowder used for blasting ore.

holidays.name: World Animal Day
holidays.description: A global day dedicated to animal welfare, where people cuddle pets, support wildlife conservation, and celebrate creatures great and small. Many shelters host adoption events and pet blessings.
holidays.origin: Started in 1925 in Berlin by Heinrich Zimmermann, a German writer, and chosen to coincide with the Feast Day of St. Francis of Assisi, the patron saint of animals.
holidays.funFact: The first World Animal Day event was held in Berlin's Sportpalast in 1925 and drew around 5,000 people.

holidays.name: National Vodka Day
holidays.description: A toast to the clear, spirited drink beloved in cocktails like the Moscow Mule and Bloody Mary. Fans celebrate by sampling new infusions and mixing up classic drinks, ideally responsibly.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American drinking holiday, popularized by spirits brands and bars. Vodka's roots stretch back to Eastern Europe, where Poland and Russia have long disputed who invented it first.
holidays.funFact: The word 'vodka' comes from the Slavic word 'voda,' meaning 'water,' so it essentially translates to 'little water.'

holidays.name: National Cinnamon Roll Day
holidays.description: A sticky, gooey, frosting-drenched celebration of the swirly pastry that makes mornings worth waking up for. Bakeries and cafes serve up warm rolls, and home bakers go all out with extra icing.
holidays.origin: Cinnamon Roll Day is celebrated in the U.S. on October 4, inspired by Sweden's Kanelbullens Dag (Cinnamon Bun Day), which was created in 1999 by the Swedish Home Baking Council to mark its 40th anniversary.
holidays.funFact: In Sweden, kanelbullar are such a cultural staple that the country celebrates Cinnamon Bun Day with national fervor, and Swedes consume them as part of the beloved coffee break tradition called 'fika.'

holidays.name: Frappe Day
holidays.description: A frosty salute to the blended, icy coffee drink that fuels students, remote workers, and caffeine lovers on hot days and cold ones alike.
holidays.origin: The frappé was reportedly invented by accident in 1957 at the Thessaloniki International Fair in Greece, when Nescafé employee Dimitris Vakondios couldn't find hot water and mixed instant coffee with cold water and ice in a shaker.
holidays.funFact: Greek frappé is made with instant coffee, and it became so iconic that it's now considered a national summer drink of Greece.
